hook.label: The Meat of the Matter · Dr Sylvia Karpagam
hook.big: The plate is never just a plate
hook.say: Food is personal. But nourishment is political. Dr Sylvia Karpagam's book, The Meat of the Matter, traces how nutrients, identity, markets and policy shape what reaches our plates.

tiles: children aged 6–59 months with some anaemia
children under six measured were stunted
infants 6–8 months fed solids on time

beats.label: 1 · Access
beats.big: Hunger is not only an empty plate
beats.say: Hunger is not only an empty plate. Between food and a nourished body sit five barriers: can it be bought, is it in the market, is it permitted, is it actually eaten, and what does the body receive?

beats.label: Access · wealth
beats.say: Wealth draws the starting line. Among children under five, {48|forty-eight} percent in the poorest households were underweight, against {19|nineteen} percent in the richest.

scene.note: 2.5× the prevalence. Income is one part of a wider system.

beats.label: Access · acceptance
beats.say: And food is also permitted, or forbidden. In NFHS five, {29|twenty-nine} percent of women and {17|seventeen} percent of men said they never ate fish, meat or eggs. Caste, religion, gender and school rules decide what is acceptable, for whom.

scene.unit: Never consume fish, meat or eggs · NFHS-5 (self-report)
scene.note: Identity and intake are different measures.

beats.label: 2 · Nutrients
beats.big: Not all protein is used the same way
beats.say: Nutrients are a system, not a score. In one study of Indian children, the body could use {87|eighty-seven} percent of the protein in egg, but about {65|sixty-five} percent in mung bean.

scene.unit: Protein digestibility in Indian children · Shivakumar et al., 2019 (study)
scene.note: Tested foods and methods only. Not a ranking of whole diets.

beats.label: Nutrients · iron and B12
beats.say: Iron in food is not iron absorbed: the meal around it and how it is cooked matter. And vitamin B12 needs a reliable source, from animal foods or fortified foods.

items: meat, poultry, fish: more readily absorbed
helps iron from grains, beans and greens
animal or fortified foods; planned vegan diets need a reliable source

beats.label: 3 · Myths
beats.say: The book tests familiar food myths. India is essentially vegetarian? Survey data show most people eat fish, meat or eggs at least sometimes. Anaemia is just iron deficiency? It has many causes.

items: Most women and men in NFHS-5 ate fish, meat or eggs at least occasionally.
Anaemia has many causes; diagnosis matters.
“Millets or soya replace every animal food.”
Valuable, but digestibility and the rest of the diet decide.

beats.label: Myths · beef
beats.say: The book argues that food restrictions are not nutrition-neutral. A {2023|twenty twenty-three} study estimated lower haemoglobin in specific beef-eating communities after beef bans.

scene.verdict: Not according to one quasi-experimental study, in specific communities.

beats.label: 4 · School meals
beats.big: A meal is made long before lunch
beats.say: A school meal is a legal entitlement. But it is made long before lunch: budget, supplier, menu, what is served, what is eaten, and what changes. The book asks: was the meal eaten and enjoyed, or only counted?

beats.label: 5 · Trade-offs
beats.say: Good food policy must weigh four things together: nutrition, climate, livelihoods, and rights and dignity. The book refuses to collapse them into one score.

beats.label: 6 · Way forward
beats.big: From the plate to the table
beats.say: The way forward: independent data, transparent funding, and real seats for students, parents, cooks and communities in deciding what is on the plate.

items: trace one nutrition claim to its original study
ask for the menu, standard and grievance contact
audit what is served, eaten and wasted
budget for whole diets; review food restrictions
